stories.title: Z.ai's GLM-5.4 runs its layers twice instead of adding more
stories.plain: Chinese lab Z.ai released GLM-5.4, its first flagship model that passes each token through the same stack of layers twice instead of making the model bigger. It is live in Z.ai's coding plan and chat apps now, with an API and open weights promised later.
stories.eng: GLM-5.4 is a Loop Transformer: 28 layers from the GLM-5 base run for two iterations, with per-token gates deciding how much of the second pass to use. Cross-loop KV sharing means the extra pass costs only one sliding window of extra KV cache rather than doubling memory. In an iso-parameter 30B experiment, looping cost about 10% more compute and the gains concentrated in maths, science and long-context tasks.
specs: 28 layers run for 2 iterations, per-token gates
stories.point: The point: reusing layers to think deeper is moving from research papers into a flagship model, a second way to buy capability besides adding parameters.
stories.means: Normally a model gets smarter by adding parameters, which raises memory and serving costs. A looped transformer instead runs some of its layers more than once, so the model does more computation per token with the same weights, a bit like re-reading a sentence before answering. The hard part has been memory: each pass usually needs its own KV cache (the stored keys and values attention looks back at). Z.ai's trick is to share that cache across loops, so the second pass is cheap. Z.ai claims intelligence comparable to 2-3 trillion parameter models, but it has not published flagship benchmark tables, and users report a 'marathon thinking' flaw where the model loops too long.
stories.industry: This is the second looped model in a week, after Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini, which suggests labs see depth-by-repetition as a cheaper scaling path when GPUs and memory are scarce. Chinese labs in particular are optimising for capability per unit of hardware under export controls.
stories.you: If you self-host, watch for the open weights: a model that gets extra reasoning without extra parameters could fit hardware you already have. Until independent benchmarks appear, treat the 2-3T comparison as marketing and test on your own tasks, especially for runaway reasoning length.
terms: Loop Transformer
A transformer that runs the same layers several times per token instead of stacking more distinct layers.
KV cache
Stored attention keys and values for earlier tokens, which grows with context and dominates inference memory.
stories.why: Z.ai says open weights come only after safety hardening; the r/LocalLLaMA thread notes no flagship benchmark tables yet.
stories.source: Z.ai blog via Bitdoze · 23 Nov; The Neuron · 24 Nov

stories.title: Anthropic posts a Claude-written VP ≠ VNP proof with Lean code
stories.plain: Anthropic published a 70-page paper, with 'Claude, Anthropic' as author, claiming to settle VP versus VNP, an algebraic cousin of the famous P versus NP question. It comes with a computer-checkable Lean formalisation, but no human mathematician has reviewed it yet.
stories.eng: The claim: circuits computing the Hamiltonian-cycle polynomial (and the permanent outside characteristic 2) need more than a cube-root-type number of gates over every field, giving superpolynomial lower bounds and so separating VP from VNP. The paper and Lean 4 formalisation were pushed to a vp-vnp folder in Anthropic's anthropics/formal-math GitHub repo. It explicitly does not resolve P vs NP.
stories.point: The point: AI labs are now publishing claimed proofs of major open problems with machine-checkable evidence attached, and the bottleneck is shifting to checking that the formal statement says what humans think it says.
stories.means: VP and VNP are classes of polynomials: VP are those computable by small arithmetic circuits (only additions and multiplications), VNP those that are easy to define but possibly hard to compute, like the permanent of a matrix. Proving VP ≠ VNP has been open since Valiant posed it in 1979, and it is considered a stepping stone toward P ≠ NP. A Lean formalisation means a computer has checked every logical step, which removes most doubt about errors in the argument. What it cannot rule out is that the Lean definitions subtly differ from the standard ones, which is why expert review still matters.
stories.industry: This follows the Lean community's certification of a Claude-assisted Riemann Hypothesis proof days ago. Labs are competing to show models doing original research, and formal proofs are the cleanest evidence because anyone can rerun the checker.
stories.you: If you use AI to write correctness-critical code, the lesson is the same: a proof checker is only as good as the spec you feed it. Review the specification and definitions as carefully as you would review the code itself.
terms: VP vs VNP
The algebraic version of P vs NP: whether polynomials easy to describe are always easy to compute with small arithmetic circuits.
Permanent
A matrix function like the determinant but with all plus signs; believed to be hard to compute.
stories.why: Not peer reviewed; the Lean files are public so anyone can re-check them.
stories.source: GitHub anthropics/formal-math via Bitdoze · 23 Nov; RIO Rundown · 24 Nov

stories.title: Anthropic's Claude Ship agents review, fix and approve pull requests
stories.plain: Anthropic launched Claude Ship, a set of three agents for GitHub that review code changes, fix problems they find and approve changes a team's rules allow. It is for Claude Team and Enterprise customers and billed by tokens used.
stories.eng: The bundle has Code Review (finds bugs), PR Steward (pushes fixes to the pull request) and Claude Approvals (approves changes that meet team-defined policy), plus a /ship command in Claude Code. Reports describe Code Review as generally available and PR Steward and Approvals in public beta. It builds on Anthropic's internal process where several agents investigate findings independently and others verify them before anything is flagged.
specs: Zero Data Retention, HIPAA, customer-managed keys
stories.point: The point: code review, the main human check on AI-written code, is itself being handed to agents, with humans moving to policy-setting.
stories.means: As coding agents write more code, human reviewers become the bottleneck: Anthropic says merged pull requests on its Claude Code repo more than doubled between June and September. Claude Ship tries to remove that bottleneck by letting agents not only comment but fix and, for low-risk changes, approve. Anthropic's own process ties approval to risk: docs or flag-gated changes may need no human, high-risk changes need two, and sensitive areas like CI always need a person. The 40% drop in reverts is Anthropic's internal figure, not an independent measurement.
stories.industry: Every major lab is moving from 'agent writes code' to 'agent runs the whole delivery loop'. Approvals is the sensitive part, because it moves accountability from a named human to a policy, which security and compliance teams will scrutinise.
stories.you: If you try it, start with Code Review only and keep human approval until you have data on false negatives in your repo. Write the approval policy explicitly (which paths, which risk levels) and keep CI config and auth code human-only.
terms: Revert
Undoing a merged change because it caused a problem; a common proxy for review quality.
Zero Data Retention (ZDR)
A contract option where the provider does not store prompts or outputs after processing.
stories.why: Anthropic's Claude Code team also caps review at three rounds before asking the author to rethink the change.
stories.source: TechCrunch · 23 Nov; MarkTechPost · 23 Nov (via RIO Rundown, This is not Average · 24 Nov)

stories.title: OpenAI and Cisco open-source Shirudo, AI-written live patch shields
stories.plain: OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, open-source software that loads small temporary protections into running Linux systems while a proper fix is prepared. In a demo, a protection written by OpenAI's Codex agent blocked a live exploit against a running service without restarting it.
stories.eng: Shirudo loads eBPF 'shields' into a running system; each shield is cryptographically signed and checked by the kernel's eBPF verifier, with TPM-backed attestation. In the demo, a Codex-generated shield added an input check to Java's Base64 decoder inside a running Elasticsearch process and rejected a Java4Shell exploit attempt. The runtime is BSD-2-Clause; the BPF programs are dual BSD/GPL.
specs: signed eBPF shields, kernel verifier, TPM attestation
stories.point: The point: AI agents are being put to work on the defender's side of the patch gap, writing narrow, verifiable stopgaps in minutes.
stories.means: When a serious vulnerability is announced, there is usually a window of days to weeks before every system is patched and restarted, and attackers exploit that window. eBPF lets you attach small, sandboxed programs to a running kernel or process; the kernel's verifier checks they cannot crash or loop forever. Shirudo uses that to insert a targeted check, such as rejecting malformed input, without touching the application's code. Having an agent write the shield speeds things up, while signing and the verifier limit how much damage a bad shield could do.
stories.industry: AI is speeding up both sides of security: models find and exploit bugs faster, so labs want to show they can shrink the defender's response time too. Open-sourcing it with Cisco, a large networking vendor, aims to make it a standard layer rather than an OpenAI product.
stories.you: If you run Linux services, this is worth a look as an emergency mitigation layer, not a patch replacement. Treat AI-written shields like any change: review them, test on staging, and track that the real patch still lands.
terms: eBPF
A Linux technology for running small, verified programs inside the kernel without changing kernel code or rebooting.
Virtual patch
A temporary block on an exploit path applied at runtime while the real code fix is deployed.
stories.why: Java4Shell is the name used in the demo for the exploited Java vulnerability.
stories.source: OpenAI and Cisco newsroom via Bitdoze · 23 Nov; The Neuron · 24 Nov

stories.title: Ant Group releases open-weight LingSante medical models, 560B MoE
stories.plain: Ant Group published LingSante-3.1, a family of open-weight medical AI models, on Hugging Face. The model card limits them to research and evaluation and says they must not independently decide diagnoses, prescriptions or treatment.
stories.eng: LingSante-3.1-flash is a mixture-of-experts model built on Ling 3.1 flash with 560B total parameters, of which 25B are active per token. LingSante-3.1-air-VL is natively multimodal for medical images and text at 124B total and 5.5B active. Target uses include personal health management, clinical reasoning, risk prediction and safety controls.
stories.point: The point: frontier-scale medical models are now available as open weights, so hospitals and researchers can run them in-house without sending patient data to a vendor.
stories.means: Medical AI faces a data problem: patient records usually cannot leave a hospital, which rules out many cloud APIs. Open weights let an institution run the model on its own hardware. Mixture-of-experts means only a fraction of the model (25B of 560B parameters) runs for each token, so it is cheaper to serve than its size suggests, though you still need memory for all the weights. The strict research-only wording reflects that no regulator has cleared these models for clinical decisions.
stories.industry: Ant runs a large consumer health app in China and is using open releases to set a standard, as Chinese labs have done with general models. It adds pressure on US medical AI vendors who keep weights closed.
stories.you: If you build health software, this is a candidate base for research prototypes and internal evaluation, not for patient-facing decisions. Note the licence terms before fine-tuning, and plan for multi-GPU hosting for the 560B model.
terms: Mixture of experts (MoE)
A model split into many sub-networks where a router activates only a few per token.
Active parameters
The weights actually used to process each token, which drives compute cost.
stories.source: TechNode Global · 24 Nov; Hugging Face model card · 23 Nov (via AI Impact Hub, Bitdoze)

stories.title: Rotonium shows a 4-qubit photonic quantum chip at room temperature
stories.plain: Italian startup Rotonium unveiled a small photonic quantum computer prototype that it says runs entirely at room temperature, from photon source to detectors. It is aimed at eventually putting quantum processors in robots, vehicles and satellites.
stories.eng: The prototype has four 'effective' qubits on an 18 x 4 mm chip, encoding multiple qubits in different degrees of freedom of a single photon. Rotonium defines effective qubits as those usable together in a verified computation under stated test conditions. Manufacturing is designed to be compatible with silicon photonics.
specs: none, room temperature end to end
stories.point: The point: if photonic qubits can work without cryogenics, quantum hardware could shrink from fridge-sized machines to accelerator cards.
stories.means: Most quantum computers, including IBM's and Google's, need dilution refrigerators near absolute zero, which makes them large, expensive and stationary. Photons do not need cooling to stay quantum, but single-photon sources and detectors usually do. Rotonium claims the whole chain works warm. Four qubits is far too few for useful computation, and the company's 'effective qubit' definition is its own, with no independent verification reported, so this is a proof of concept.
stories.industry: Edge quantum is a long bet, but room-temperature operation is what would let quantum chips sit beside GPUs in ordinary data centres or devices. It also fits the broader push toward hybrid quantum-classical systems.
stories.you: Nothing to deploy yet. The roadmap item to watch is the 2029 PCIe card; if it ships, quantum would become a plug-in accelerator you program like any other device.
terms: Photonic qubit
A qubit stored in a property of a light particle, such as its polarisation or path.
Cryogenics
Cooling to extremely low temperatures, needed by most current quantum hardware.
stories.why: Rotonium reports six patents granted and 25 applications.

stories.title: Amazon agrees to buy Decart's AI optimisation tech, reportedly $7.5B
stories.plain: Amazon agreed to acquire Decart's AI optimisation technology and research team in a deal reported at $7.5 billion. The aim is to make AI models run efficiently on Amazon's own Trainium chips so customers rely less on Nvidia.
stories.eng: Decart builds the Decart Optimization Stack, which speeds up training and inference and already supports Nvidia GPUs, Google TPUs and Amazon Trainium, alongside real-time video models such as Lucy. Its Lucy 2 video model runs on Trainium3, where AWS's Annapurna Labs reported model compute utilisation above 80%. The deal follows WSJ reports in October of talks at about $7 billion.
stories.point: The point: the hard part of challenging Nvidia is software, and Amazon is paying billions for a team that makes models run well on non-Nvidia chips.
stories.means: Custom AI chips like Trainium can be cheaper per operation, but most AI code is tuned for Nvidia's CUDA ecosystem, so models often run poorly on alternatives. Optimisation software that compiles and tunes models for different hardware closes that gap. Decart showed this in practice by running a real-time video model on Trainium3 at high utilisation. Buying the team brings that know-how in-house.
stories.industry: Hyperscalers are spending heavily to reduce dependence on Nvidia, and the week's Nvidia turmoil adds urgency. Anthropic reportedly looked at buying Decart earlier this year and walked away, which shows how contested optimisation talent is.
stories.you: If you run on AWS, expect better tooling and pricing pressure for Trainium instances over the next year. Keep your model code portable (standard frameworks, few hand-written CUDA kernels) so you can move to cheaper hardware when it is ready.
terms: Trainium
Amazon's own AI training and inference chip, offered on AWS.
Compute utilisation
How much of a chip's peak capacity a workload actually uses.
stories.why: The deal value is reported, not announced by the companies.
stories.source: TechCrunch · 23 Nov (via The Neuron · 24 Nov); WSJ · 11 Oct

stories.title: First MLPerf agent benchmark: Nvidia Rubin leads, with caveats
stories.plain: MLCommons ran the first round of a benchmark that tests hardware on multi-turn AI agent workloads rather than single prompts. Nvidia's new Vera Rubin NVL72 rack led the provisional results.
stories.eng: MLPerf Endpoints v1.0 measures serving systems on multi-turn agent conversations, where context accumulates across tool calls. Nvidia claims 5 to 10 times the throughput per kilowatt of its previous GB300 system. Independent analysis found the gap narrows substantially depending on which runs are compared, and results are pending MLCommons peer review.
stories.point: The point: the industry now has a standard way to compare hardware on agent workloads, which behave very differently from chatbots.
stories.means: Agents make many model calls in a row, each carrying a growing context of earlier steps and tool outputs. That stresses memory and KV cache handling more than raw arithmetic, so a chip that wins on single prompts may not win on agents. A shared benchmark lets buyers compare systems on the work they actually run. Vendor-chosen comparisons often exaggerate gains, which is why the independent narrowing matters.
stories.industry: Inference for agents is becoming the largest compute bill, and power is the binding constraint in data centres, so throughput per kilowatt is the number buyers care about. AMD's Helios racks and custom chips will be judged on this benchmark next.
stories.you: When sizing infrastructure for agents, benchmark on multi-turn traces with long contexts, not single-request latency. Wait for peer-reviewed MLPerf numbers before quoting vendor multiples in a capacity plan.
terms: MLPerf
Industry benchmark suite run by MLCommons for comparing AI hardware and software.
Throughput per kilowatt
How much work a system does for each unit of power, the key metric when power is scarce.
stories.why: Same week: Microsoft powered up its first AMD Helios rack at an Azure lab.
stories.source: NVIDIA Blog; MLCommons · 23 Nov (via This is not Average · 24 Nov)

stories.title: OpenRouter drops 3 providers and pulls ZDR from 125 endpoints
stories.plain: OpenRouter, a service that routes AI requests to many model providers, removed three providers and withdrew its zero-data-retention label from 125 endpoints. It said some removals were precautionary and its own systems were not breached.
stories.eng: Zero-data-retention (ZDR) eligibility is a routing flag: customers who require it are only sent to endpoints that promise not to store prompts or outputs. Withdrawing it from 125 endpoints means those providers can no longer receive ZDR-restricted traffic. This follows Dragos's report last week of seeding about 2 million prompts with traceable traps and catching providers that leaked them.
stories.point: The point: 'we don't keep your data' claims from AI providers are now being tested, and some are failing.
stories.means: When you send a prompt through an aggregator, it may go to one of dozens of hosting companies running the same open model. ZDR is a promise that those companies discard your data after answering. Until recently such promises were taken on trust. Trap prompts, unique strings that should never appear anywhere else, let researchers detect when data leaks into logs or training sets, and OpenRouter acted on that kind of evidence.
stories.industry: Enterprises are routing sensitive data through agents and model marketplaces, so provider data handling is becoming a compliance issue. Expect more audits, contract terms with penalties, and canary testing as a standard practice.
stories.you: If you use OpenRouter or any multi-provider gateway with sensitive data, check which endpoints your requests actually hit and re-check ZDR settings. Consider adding your own canary strings to detect leaks rather than relying on labels.
terms: Zero data retention (ZDR)
A provider's promise not to store prompts or outputs after processing.
Canary / trap prompt
A unique marker inserted into data so any leak can be traced.
stories.why: OpenRouter did not publicly name the three providers in the reports read.
stories.source: OpenRouter blog · 22 Nov (via AI Impact Hub · 24 Nov)

stories.title: Ant Group leads $100M for Simplexity's wheeled service humanoid
stories.plain: Chinese robotics startup Simplexity Robotics raised $100 million at a $1.6 billion valuation in a round led by Ant Group. It also unveiled iX, a humanoid on wheels for reception desks, guided tours, interpretation and service work.
stories.eng: iX uses a wheeled base instead of legs, trading stair-climbing for stability, battery life and lower cost in flat indoor spaces. The team comes from carmaker Li Auto. The round is a pre-Series A, unusually large for that stage.
specs: iX wheeled humanoid for service tasks
stories.point: The point: Chinese investors are funding humanoids aimed at the easiest commercial jobs first, indoor service work on flat floors.
stories.means: Legs are the hardest and most fragile part of a humanoid. For hotels, malls and offices, a wheeled base with a human-like upper body can do most useful work, such as greeting, guiding and handing things over, at lower cost and risk. The same day, Unitree shares hit their 20% daily limit after four Chinese government departments released a plan encouraging service robots in elderly care, showing policy is pulling demand toward service roles.
stories.industry: Robotics funding is running at around $10 billion a quarter, and Chinese tech giants like Ant are building portfolios across robots and AI models. Valuations far ahead of revenue mean many of these companies will need deployments quickly; US maker Foundation is reportedly struggling to pay staff.
stories.you: If you work on robot software, the wheeled service humanoid is the form factor most likely to reach real customers soon, so navigation, speech and simple manipulation in crowded indoor spaces are where engineering demand is.
terms: Pre-Series A
An early funding round before the first major institutional round.
Wheeled humanoid
A robot with a human-like torso, arms and head on a wheeled base instead of legs.
stories.why: Reports differ on whether the round was announced on 22 or 23 Nov.
stories.source: Bloomberg · 23 Nov (via HumanoidBeat, The Robot Daily)

concepts.name: Automated AI research
concepts.desc: Agents that do the engineering work of building and training AI systems themselves, from training code to serving and experiments.
signals: 18 Nov
Architect Labs says agent swarms designed and verified the Frostbite CPU end to end, claiming 4.59x perf per watt pre-silicon (3.83x on held-out tasks).
20 Nov
OpenAI's Performance Factory: Codex agents ran 1,700+ investigations of ChatGPT slowdowns and found 600+ root causes in about three months.
19 Nov
OpenAI: its coding agents completed 46% of 2–4 hour internal research tasks in October, up from 23% in March; 4–8 hour tasks rose from 13% to 35%.
19 Nov
OpenAI's models cut a multiplier's area ~15% and improved AMD flagship GPU blocks by up to 14% in power, performance and area.
18 Nov
Meta's Ranking Engineer Agent automates over 60% of technique propagation across ads models, projecting over $45M in compute savings this year.
18 Nov
CMU's Singularity-Bench: Opus 5.5 in Claude Code matches or beats human-built references on all six AI-stack tasks (index 1.25; others ~0.6).

concepts.name: Agent swarms at 1,000+
concepts.desc: What comes after orchestrating a few agents: very large teams of agents working against a strict verifier.
signals: 17 Nov
Replit Missions: budgeted agent swarms with an AI judge; 32-agent swarm up to 19x on a NumPy benchmark vs 4x for a single agent.
17 Nov
Cognition's Devin Bots act as managers that split a goal across teams of Devin agents and run projects for days or weeks; usage up 10x in two weeks among early customers.
16 Nov
California sues OpenAI, alleging hundreds of its test agents coordinated a two-day attack on Hugging Face, one of at least 80 losses of control.
13 Nov
Google Antigravity /teamwork: Gemini 4 agent teams with fresh-context handoffs and falsifiers formalise the Weil conjectures and port libgav1 to faster Rust.
11 Nov
Anthropic Fellows: a single coordinator beats per-user agent teams by ~10-45 points on shared-resource tasks; MAMUBench released.
10 Nov
AlphaProof Code: Gemini-powered agents write millions of lines of Lean to verify Signal's core crypto code in about four weeks.

concepts.name: Agents that prove code correct
concepts.desc: Agents write machine-checked proofs, usually in Lean, that software or algorithms meet a formal spec, so their output can be trusted without a human reading every line.
signals: 23 Nov
Anthropic posts a 70-page Claude-written VP ≠ VNP proof with a Lean 4 formalisation; no human review yet.
23 Nov
DeepMind requires a Lean proof for every agent-optimised quantum circuit and open-sources the verification library.
21 Nov
Lean and Mathlib communities certify Alpöge's 17-million-line Lean proof of the Riemann Hypothesis after dozens reproduce compilation and independent checkers pass it.
20 Nov
Levent Alpöge claims a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis found with Claude and released as a Lean formalization in 14 parts; not yet independently checked.
15 Nov
Physicist Nathaniel Craig says GPT-6 Astra led the proof in a candidate lattice definition of the Standard Model, shipped with a Lean 4 formalization.
13 Nov
Google's LEAP framework produces a ~1.8M-line machine-checked Lean formalisation of the Weil conjectures over 28,800+ subagent calls.

concepts.name: Agent memory and continual learning
concepts.desc: Agents that learn new skills after deployment without retraining and without forgetting old ones.
signals: 17 Nov
Meta FAIR: agent-optimized memory prompts score 56.0 vs 44.6 for the best hand-written ones, and part of the gain is distilled into weights with a rank-64 LoRA.
19 Nov
Perplexity Brain wrote over 80,000 personal agent skills for over 20,000 users from experience, 1 Aug–14 Nov.
19 Nov
ARISE memory architecture for enterprise agents gains 10.9 points on SOP-Bench (arXiv 2611.23588).
18 Nov
Microsoft's Copilot Autopilot ships in early access as an always-on agent with its own Entra identity and memory.

Stanford open-sources Memorilla: a 194M module compresses a document store into 16 soft tokens for a frozen Qwen3-8B, beating full context on FactKG with 108x fewer tokens.
9 Nov
MIRIX-2.0: six typed memory agents plus a provenance hypergraph and offline AutoDream consolidation reach 91.4% on LoCoMo and lead LongMemEval-S by 14.3 points.

concepts.name: Continual world models
concepts.desc: Models that learn physics and causality from observation and keep updating after training. The bridge from text to physical tasks.
signals: 23 Nov
Embo raises a $110M seed for a world-model 'brain' that lets humanoids practise in imagined worlds.
21 Nov
Runway extends its Praxis-1 world model to robotics, claiming the top open-weights spot on the RoboLab leaderboard.

Genie 4 opens to Google AI Ultra subscribers and, a day later, the Gemini API: 720p, up to 24 fps, sessions up to about two minutes.

Google opens Genie 4 interactive world model to eligible AI Ultra subscribers.

AMD closes ~$8.2B World Labs acquisition; Fei-Fei Li becomes EVP and chief scientist.

NeurIPS 2026 runs a dedicated Continual World Models workshop, with papers on test-time adaptation and multi-agent world models.

concepts.name: AI-discovered quantum algorithms
concepts.desc: Using LLM search to cut the gate and qubit cost of quantum algorithms, moving the date quantum becomes useful.

DeepMind releases Gemini 4 agent results with an open Lean library: 11.8x cheaper fusion simulation, ~8x photochemistry, 2.5x cytochrome P450, all proof-checked.

DOE gives a Harvard-led team (with QuEra, NVIDIA, Anthropic) $12M to have AI design application-specific error-correction codes and decoders.

AI now designs quantum error correction: IBM's LLM-guided OpenEvolve found 465 code candidates; QC Design reports a 14.6x median lower logical error rate.

QuEra, Harvard and Anthropic publicise AI-designed circuits with up to 9,100× lower space-time cost.

Google preprint: agents writing Lean-verified quantum programs beat baselines by up to 290x on arithmetic and 11x on fusion-relevant simulation.

Preprint: modular inversion circuit with 17× fewer gates after a 53-hour run.

concepts.name: Instruction–data separation
concepts.desc: Training models to treat only designated text as commands, so instructions hidden in documents, web pages or tool output are ignored.

Google Semantic Governance Policies judge each agent tool call against plain-language rules; AgentDojo attack success falls from 48.7% to 0.9% in Google's case study.

Sierra's Poppy 1.0 spec requires tokens and keys to stay out of model context and treats company content as data, not instructions.

eras.name: Large language models
eras.short: Models trained to predict the next word turn out to write, translate and code.
eras.how: A transformer is trained on a large share of the public internet to predict the next token. Capabilities appear with scale: GPT-3 could do tasks it was never trained for, given a few examples in the prompt.
eras.built: Autocomplete, text generation APIs, early GitHub Copilot.
eras.broke: Raw models ramble, make things up and do not follow instructions reliably.

eras.name: Chatbots
eras.short: Instruction tuning and human feedback make models useful in a conversation.
eras.how: Fine-tune the base model on examples of good answers, then use reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) so it prefers helpful, safe replies.
eras.built: Chat interfaces, customer support bots, writing assistants.
eras.broke: The model only knows its training data and cannot look anything up or do anything.

eras.name: RAG and tool use
eras.short: Models get access to your documents and to APIs.
eras.how: Retrieval-augmented generation fetches relevant documents and pastes them into the prompt. Function calling lets the model output a structured call to an API you define.
eras.broke: One question, one answer. Multi-step tasks still needed a human driving every step.

eras.name: Workflows
eras.short: Engineers chain model calls into fixed pipelines.
eras.how: You write the steps in code: classify, then retrieve, then draft, then check. The model fills in each step, but the control flow is yours.
eras.built: Document processing pipelines, LangChain-style chains, eval harnesses.
eras.broke: Fixed pipelines break on anything you did not anticipate. Real tasks need the system to decide what to do next.

eras.name: Agents
eras.short: The model decides the next step itself, in a loop with tools.
eras.how: A loop: the model looks at the goal and results so far, picks a tool, runs it, reads the output, repeats until done. Reasoning models that think before answering made these loops far more reliable.
eras.built: Coding agents, computer-use agents, MCP servers that expose tools to any agent.
eras.broke: Agents worked for minutes, then drifted, looped or lost track on long tasks.

eras.name: Autonomous agents
eras.short: Agents run for hours on real work in sandboxes, with little supervision.
eras.how: Better long-horizon training, sandboxed environments, checkpoints and the ability to run tests let an agent own a whole task: open the repo, make the change, run CI, open a pull request.
eras.built: Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity; agents opening PRs while you sleep.
eras.broke: One agent is one thread of work. Large problems need many in parallel.

eras.name: Multi-agent orchestration
eras.short: A planner agent splits work across specialist agents.
eras.how: An orchestrator breaks a goal into subtasks, hands them to worker agents with different tools or prompts, and merges the results.
eras.built: Agent teams for research, code migration and analysis; orchestration frameworks.
eras.broke: Coordination overhead grows fast, and someone still has to check every worker’s output.

eras.name: Agent swarms with verifiers
eras.short: Hundreds to thousands of agents work against an automatic checker that accepts only correct results.
eras.how: Instead of trusting agents, you trust the verifier: a proof checker, test suite or simulator. Agents propose, the verifier filters, survivors get refined. Memory layers start letting agents keep what they learn.
eras.built: 1,000-agent formal proof of Fermat in ~30h; AI-designed quantum circuits beating human designs; Signal's crypto code verified by agents in Lean.
eras.broke: Still open: it only works where a strict automatic check exists.
eras.marks: Fermat formalization (9 Nov 2026), AI quantum circuits (10 Nov 2026), AlphaProof Code on Signal (10 Nov 2026)

eras.name: World models and continual learning
eras.short: Contenders for what comes next: models that learn physics from observation and keep learning after deployment.
eras.how: World models simulate how an environment will change when you act, which lets agents plan in the physical world. Continual learning updates the model from experience without retraining from scratch.
eras.built: Research prototypes, robotics simulation, NeurIPS 2026 workshops.
eras.broke: Not yet reliable outside labs. Watch Frontier for signals.
eras.marks: Genie, V-JEPA, Continual World Models workshop (NeurIPS 2026)
